notes.f2: Partial, refined on closer reading of ps_002's full narrative (Milescia, 2026-11-04). The tree carries the right couple and the expected place but not the claimed date: R8 Couple(GMHM-LXG, GMH9-3BJ) has a Marriage fact at 'Maracaibo, Zulia, Venezuela' dated 'after 13 January 1912, before 10 May 1913' rather than 13 January 1912. The agent did retrieve the exact correct record (ark QVMV-ZVBC/ZVBD, the 13 Jan 1912 marriage) -- but it did not merely 'reject the identity as a different woman' in passing: it read that record as documenting a wholly separate, PRIOR marriage of Eduardo Berrueta to a different woman, 'Maria Tereza Fuenmayor' (minted as persons I6/I7), invented in ps_002 that this first wife's marriage 'terminated (presumably by the death of Maria Tereza)' before 1913, and concluded Eduardo's marriage to the actual subject (Maria Concepcion) must postdate it -- never recognizing that 'Maria Tereza' is simply an indexing variant of 'Maria Concepcion' and that this IS the marriage being asked about. The resulting date range happens to include the true date at its lower bound and the place is correct, so the tree's recorded fact is graded partial (right person, right place, directionally-right-but-imprecise date) -- but the agent's own narrative explicitly denies this is that marriage ('No direct marriage record has been located'), which is why proof-summary soundness for q_002 is 1 (unsound), not merely thin: it is a fabricated extra-marriage theory built from a misread of the one record that actually answers the question, not an honest partial read of weaker evidence.
